clue.text: Modern December 25th?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the current era
second meaning, read literally: Christmas Day is the day for gifts

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: the hyphenated adjective split into a day when gifts are given.
explanation.definitionFit: Present-day as an adjective means current or contemporary; whimsically, Christmas is the gift-giving day.

clue.text: Quiz machine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to question someone persistently for information
second meaning: a device that moves liquid or air

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub quiz machine, but the two words are separate meanings, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate someone insistently is to pump them; a pump is also a mechanical device for moving fluids.

clue.text: Treat nine to spread in harbour

indicators.note: letters that spread out are scattered and can settle into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone treats nine people to a dockside spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' looks like the definition (entertain does mean treat), but it is fodder; the definition is 'harbour' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a thought or hope is to entertain it, keeping it in mind as a possibility.

clue.text: Neil's friend, oddly cast resembling one of Santa's helpers?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are cast away, so only the even ones survive

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A friend of Neil's has been strangely cast as a Christmas elf in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means thrown out: the odd letters are discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate like an elf, and elves are traditionally Father Christmas's workshop assistants.

clue.text: Magazine published after interval

indicators.note: after tells us the first word comes behind the second in the finished answer

parts.note: a period or interval of time
a book that is published is out

explanation.surface: A magazine issue is released after a break in production.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME OUT is a London listings and entertainment magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Time Out is the title of a well-known city listings publication, so it is an example of a magazine.

clue.text: Claims adult is undermined by tension returning

indicators.note: in a down clue, something undermined has the next part sitting beneath it

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: stress is strain or tension

explanation.surface: Someone claims a grown-up is being worn down by mounting tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserts is a verb meaning states firmly, matching claims as a third-person present verb.

clue.text: Somewhat overpriced oven-ready bird

indicators.note: somewhat means only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and first three of the second

explanation.surface: A supermarket bird, prepared for roasting, is rather expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A dove is a type of bird of the pigeon family, so the definition is a general category.

clue.text: Going up, regularly forgot Luton will generate expenditure

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, backwards
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone forgot about Luton, and rising costs will follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is a town north of London with an airport, offered as a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgo is money going out, an outlay or expense; the word is a rarer twin of outgoings.

clue.text: Holly and Ivy maybe exposed retreat politician visits

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so this word is placed within the other
exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: to reverse is to go backwards or retreat
a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: A politician visits a Christmas grotto with holly and ivy on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Exposing a word strips its first and last letters; the politician then sits inside the remainder just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly and ivy keep their leaves all winter, so they are examples of plants that stay green year-round.

clue.text: Test whether to show design on clothing

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
if and whether are interchangeable in 'ask if/whether'

explanation.surface: Someone tests whether a printed pattern works on a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety check required for older cars in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a decorative image or pattern, often appliquéd or printed on a garment.

clue.text: Criminal stole item that's obtained for a smacker?

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief pinched something acquired for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A smacker is slang both for a pound and for a loud kiss; the second sense is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition says people standing under hung sprigs of this plant must kiss, so it is put up to win a smacker.

clue.text: Comparatively young darts player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: smaller, the comparative of little, used of children
second meaning: Luke ..., the English teenage world darts champion

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a youthful darts player, apt as Luke Littler won the world title aged seventeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Littler, comparative of little, is used for younger children; Luke Littler is a famous professional darts thrower.

clue.text: Managed to attend tribunal, no time for bitterness

indicators.note: no time says the usual abbreviation for time must be taken out

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a court is a tribunal

explanation.surface: Someone made it to a tribunal hearing but had no time to spare for resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time, removed from COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment or ill will, a synonym for bitterness.

clue.text: Ruffian's working to replace posh undergarment

indicators.note: to replace means one element is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: a ruffian is a thug; the 's means 'has'
a machine that is working is on
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A thug is busy replacing some fancy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: ON replaces the U in THUG. U for upper-class is a crossword convention from the 'U and non-U' debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is skimpy underwear with a narrow strip at the back, one kind of undergarment.

clue.text: Sorts of cars Spooner's set copes with

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don notorious for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a set is a batch, and to copes with something is to hack it; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: Someone describes which kinds of cars a family copes with.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'hack it' is informal for to cope; the swapped pair is the clue's whole mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a car style with a rear door hinged at the top, so the plural names several types of car.

clue.text: Resisting using cooker this month?

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy range cooker
inst., short for instant, means 'of this month' in old business letters

explanation.surface: Someone is resisting using the oven this month, perhaps over the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the preposition of opposition, as in being against an idea, matching resisting.

clue.text: Mostly unnecessary things dropped during the festive season?

definitions.text: things dropped during the festive season?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

explanation.surface: Christmas brings largely pointless items that get shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: real Christmas trees shed their pine spines on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut fir indoors sheds its leaves, called needles, all over the floor by the end of the holidays.

clue.text: Rescue of American, 55, Herb inspires

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one part is taken inside another

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
A is a standard abbreviation for American
55 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An American aged 55 is rescued by someone called Herb who inspires him.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is the rescue of goods or a ship from loss, so as a noun it is a synonym for rescue.

clue.text: Examining a line in some carol

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of letters inside the following word

parts.note: some and any are both indefinite quantity words
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone is studying a single line within a Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like part of the picture, but here it is a verb meaning to sing joyfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysing means scrutinising something closely, part by part, so it matches examining as a present participle.

clue.text: Maintain nurse is backing Tory

indicators.note: backing here means coming behind and supporting from the rear, so it is placed second

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A nurse supports the Conservative candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend that something is so is to maintain or assert it in argument.

clue.text: Problem with excerpt from programme Lidington raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted bottom to top, so the letters read backwards
an excerpt is a piece lifted from a longer text

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A clip from a show featuring Lidington raised a difficult issue.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lidington is a former British Conservative minister; his name is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, a kind of problem.

clue.text: Special offer in pub once more, starter discounted

indicators.note: the opening letter is knocked off, as a discount knocks something off a price

parts.note: a bar is a pub
again means once more

explanation.surface: A pub is running a discounted deal on starters again.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something bought cheaply, the result of a sale price or promotion.

clue.text: Prizefighter rues rib getting broken

indicators.note: broken things are smashed apart, and these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxer regrets having a rib cracked in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is a big tough fighter, informally a boxer, so it fits prizefighter.

clue.text: British student welcomes campaign about scrap

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so the outer pair holds another part

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: a war is a military campaign
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A British student hosts a campaign group on a topic of scrapping something.
explanation.walkthrough: B and L together surround WAR read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informal for a fight, and a brawl is a rough noisy fight.

clue.text: Time of year interest rate primarily impacts pound

parts.note: APR is annual percentage rate

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter
L, from Latin libra, is the pound symbol

explanation.surface: A season when an interest rate mainly affects sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a month, and a month is a period or time of year.

clue.text: Around noon periodically clear up dirty clothes for washing

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the selected letters go round the next one
periodically means at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these three words
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: At about midday, someone regularly tidies dirty clothes for the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' looks like part of the definition but is fodder for the alternate letters; LAUDRY goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is the collective word for clothes and linen waiting to be washed.

clue.text: Cook with spicy seasoning continued being revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: lived on means continued existing

explanation.surface: A cook kept making radical, highly spiced dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To devil food, such as kidneys or eggs, is to prepare it with hot condiments like mustard or cayenne.

clue.text: Pay for turkey perhaps when picked up

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: turkey is an example of flesh eaten as food

explanation.surface: Someone pays for the Christmas turkey when collecting it from the butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a bill or cost is to settle it, so it means pay for.

clue.text: Noel and Charlie graduate wearing scruffy shirts

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one part goes within the other
scruffy means untidy, so the letters are messed up into new order

parts.note: taken as written
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Two men, Noel and Charlie, one a graduate, wear untidy shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noel' reads like a man's name next to Charlie; it is the definition. MA goes inside the rearranged shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is an old word for the festive season of December, from the French for the nativity feast.

clue.text: Corruption envelops old singer

indicators.note: envelops means wraps round, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: vice is wickedness or corruption
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Corruption surrounds an ageing performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer can be called a voice, as in a choir needing another tenor voice.

clue.text: KC ultimately seems kind

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter
ilk means sort or kind

explanation.surface: A King's Counsel appears, in the end, to be a decent sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A KC, King's Counsel, is a senior barrister in Britain, who wears a silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior barristers are informally called silks after their gowns; becoming a KC is 'taking silk'.

clue.text: Steps taken to acquire fresh tree decoration

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps
a fresh, breezy room is airy

explanation.surface: Climbing the stairs to fetch a fresh ornament for the Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is usually plural; here the enumeration asks for the singular form of the bulb strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy lights are small strings of electric bulbs hung on a Christmas tree, so one is a festive ornament.
